points.description: Classification is described as mapping data to discrete labels or categories (equivalent wording is fine, e.g. predicting a class).

Regression is described as mapping data to continuous values or real numbers, and the answer makes clear this is the difference from classification (equivalent wording is fine, e.g. predicting a quantity).

deductions.description: Says regression outputs discrete labels or classes, or says classification outputs continuous values (the two are swapped).

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) for stating that classification predicts discrete labels/categories and regression predicts continuous real-valued outputs. The error-metric detail in the model answer (misclassification count vs summed distance) is not required by the question and is not marked. A correct statement of only one side earns 1 mark; swapping the two sides loses the mark for that side.
